title: Proverbs Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Proverbs 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A wise son maketh a glad father
The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life
He that gathereth in summer is a wise son
The LORD will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish
questions.correctAnswer: A wise son maketh a glad father
questions.explanation: This phrase appears first in the chapter, establishing the contrast between a wise son and a foolish son.

questions.question: What do treasures of wickedness profit according to Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: The verse states that treasures of wickedness profit nothing, emphasizing the futility of wicked gains.

questions.question: What will the LORD not suffer according to Proverbs 10?
options: The soul of the wicked to flourish
The soul of the righteous to famish
The body of the righteous to suffer
The heart of the foolish to be glad
questions.correctAnswer: The soul of the righteous to famish
questions.explanation: This verse clearly states that the LORD will not allow the soul of the righteous to go hungry.

questions.question: What does the diligent hand do according to Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the hand of the diligent maketh rich, contrasting with the slack hand.

questions.question: Who is considered a wise son in Proverbs 10?
options: He that winketh with the eye
questions.explanation: The verse states that he who gathers in summer is a wise son, indicating preparedness and diligence.

questions.question: What covers the mouth of the wicked in Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: This verse states that violence covers the mouth of the wicked, indicating their corrupt nature.

questions.question: What is said about the memory of the just in Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: According to this verse, the memory of the just is blessed, highlighting their positive legacy.

questions.question: What will the wise in heart receive according to Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: This verse states that the wise in heart will receive commandments, emphasizing their willingness to learn.

questions.question: What happens to he that walketh uprightly according to Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: The verse confirms that he that walketh uprightly walketh surely, indicating stability and security.

questions.question: What does he that winketh with the eye cause according to Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: This verse indicates that winking with the eye causes sorrow, highlighting the consequences of deceit.

questions.question: What is the mouth of a righteous man compared to in Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the mouth of a righteous man is a well of life, signifying the positive impact of their words.

questions.question: True or False: A wise son makes a glad father.
questions.explanation: This statement is directly supported by Proverbs 10:1, where it describes the joy a wise son brings to his father.

questions.question: True or False: The righteous will suffer hunger.
questions.explanation: According to Proverbs 10:3, the LORD will not allow the soul of the righteous to famish, indicating they will not suffer hunger.

questions.question: True or False: The name of the wicked shall be blessed.
questions.explanation: This is incorrect as Proverbs 10:7 states that the name of the wicked shall rot, indicating a negative legacy.

questions.question: True or False: The mouth of a wicked man is a source of life.
questions.explanation: This statement is false because Proverbs 10:11 states that the mouth of a righteous man is a well of life, not the wicked.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 10:12, what effect does love have on sins?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:12 states that 'love covereth all sins,' meaning love can forgive or overlook faults.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 10:13 promise will happen if someone has understanding according to Proverbs 10:12?
options: Wisdom is found in their lips
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is found in their lips
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:13 states that 'In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found,' which follows from the love overcoming hatred in 10:12.

questions.question: What is described as a 'strong city' for the rich man in Proverbs 10?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:15 says 'The rich man's wealth is his strong city,' indicating wealth provides security.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 10:17 relate to Proverbs 10:18 in terms of behavior and consequences?
options: Keeping instruction leads to life; hiding hatred with lies shows foolishness
Refusing reproof brings blessings; loving covers sins
Wise lips bring destruction; fools hide hatred
Labor of the righteous leads to poverty; wicked fruit leads to life
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping instruction leads to life; hiding hatred with lies shows foolishness
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:17 teaches that keeping instruction leads to life, while 10:18 warns that hiding hatred with lying lips is foolish, showing cause and effect of obedience versus deceit.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 10:16, what is the outcome of the labor of the righteous compared to the fruit of the wicked?
options: Life for the righteous; sin for the wicked
Poverty for the righteous; wealth for the wicked
Destruction for the righteous; blessing for the wicked
Sorrow for the righteous; joy for the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Life for the righteous; sin for the wicked
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:16 says 'The labour of the righteous tendeth to life: but the fruit of the wicked to sin,' indicating the contrasting results of their deeds.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 10:19 suggest about the use of words?
options: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin
questions.correctAnswer: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:19 warns that many words often contain sin, advocating restraint in speech.

questions.question: What is the value of the tongue of the just according to Proverbs 10:20?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:20 compares the tongue of the just to choice silver, emphasizing its preciousness and value.

questions.question: How do the lips of the righteous affect others according to Proverbs 10:21?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:21 states that 'The lips of the righteous feed many,' indicating their words provide nourishment and encouragement.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 10:22 say about the blessing of the LORD?
options: It maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it
It is only for the poor
questions.correctAnswer: It maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:22 teaches that the blessing of the LORD enriches without bringing sorrow, a true and lasting blessing.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 10:14, what do wise men do with knowledge?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:14 says 'Wise men lay up knowledge,' meaning they store and preserve it carefully.

questions.question: What consequence does Proverbs 10:21 associate with fools lacking wisdom?
options: They die for want of wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: They die for want of wisdom
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:21 states that fools die for lack of wisdom, emphasizing the vital importance of wisdom for life.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 10:18 say about a person who hides hatred with lying lips?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:18 clearly states that he who hides hatred with lying lips is a fool, showing the folly of deceit.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 10:22 teaches that the blessing of the LORD brings sorrow along with riches.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:22 says the blessing of the LORD 'maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it,' indicating no sorrow accompanies the blessing.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 10:17 indicates that refusing reproof causes a person to err.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:17 states 'he that refuseth reproof erreth,' making this statement true.

questions.question: True or False: According to Proverbs 10:19, speaking many words is always wise.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:19 warns that 'in the multitude of words there wanteth not sin,' so many words are not always wise.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 10.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 10:23, how does a man of understanding differ from a fool in their approach to mischief?
options: A man of understanding hath wisdom, but it is as sport to a fool to do mischief
Both a fool and a man of understanding delight equally in mischief
A fool has wisdom, but a man of understanding enjoys mischief
Neither a fool nor a man of understanding engage in mischief
questions.correctAnswer: A man of understanding hath wisdom, but it is as sport to a fool to do mischief
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:23 states, 'It is as sport to a fool to do mischief: but a man of understanding hath wisdom,' showing the contrast in attitude toward wrongdoing.

questions.question: What is the contrast in outcomes described in Proverbs 10:24 between the wicked and the righteous?
options: The fear of the wicked shall come upon him; the desire of the righteous shall be granted
The wicked shall prosper; the righteous shall suffer
Both wicked and righteous will have their desires fulfilled
The righteous shall fear, but the wicked shall be fearless
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of the wicked shall come upon him; the desire of the righteous shall be granted
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:24 clearly states the fearful consequence for the wicked and the fulfillment for the righteous desires.

questions.question: In Proverbs 10:25, what simile is used to describe the fate of the wicked compared to the righteous?
options: As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more; but the righteous is an everlasting foundation
As a rock stands firm, so the wicked endure; but the righteous vanish like smoke
As a shadow fades, the righteous disappear; but the wicked are like a storm
The wicked are like a tree planted by rivers; the righteous are like chaff
questions.correctAnswer: As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more; but the righteous is an everlasting foundation
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:25 uses the simile of a whirlwind to describe the swift removal of the wicked, contrasting it to the enduring foundation of the righteous.

questions.question: How is the sluggard described in Proverbs 10:26 and what effect does he have on those who send him?
options: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes; he is unpleasant to those who send him
Like honey to the soul; he refreshes those who send him
Like a shadow at noon; he is unnoticed by those who send him
Like a gentle breeze; he soothes those who send him
questions.correctAnswer: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes; he is unpleasant to those who send him
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:26 compares the sluggard to vinegar and smoke, indicating the irritation and displeasure he causes to those who employ him.

questions.question: What effect does the fear of the LORD have according to Proverbs 10:27?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:27 states 'The fear of the LORD prolongeth days,' indicating a life-extending blessing for the godly.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 10:28, what is the fate of the hope and expectation of the righteous and the wicked respectively?
options: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness; the expectation of the wicked shall perish
Both the hope of the righteous and the wicked shall perish
The hope of the righteous shall perish; the expectation of the wicked shall be gladness
Both the hope of the righteous and the wicked shall be gladness
questions.correctAnswer: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness; the expectation of the wicked shall perish
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:28 contrasts the positive outcome of the righteous's hope with the perishing expectation of the wicked.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ḥāmad' (חמד) in Proverbs 10:24 mean?
questions.explanation: In Proverbs 10:24, the Hebrew word 'ḥāmad' means 'desire,' referring to what the righteous long for being granted.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified in Proverbs 10:25 with the comparison of the wicked to a whirlwind and the righteous to an everlasting foundation?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:25 uses antithetical parallelism contrasting the fleeting wicked with the enduring righteous foundation.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Proverbs 10:27 about the fear of the LORD prolonging life?
options: 1 John 4:18 - Perfect love casts out fear
Romans 8:15 - For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear
Ecclesiastes 12:13 - Fear God and keep his commandments
Hebrews 12:28 - Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved
questions.correctAnswer: Ecclesiastes 12:13 - Fear God and keep his commandments
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 12:13 similarly emphasizes fearing God and keeping His commandments, resonating with Proverbs 10:27's theme of reverence to the LORD prolonging life.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse connects with Proverbs 10:29 about the way of the LORD being strength to the upright?
options: Psalm 18:32 - God is my strength and power
Isaiah 53:5 - By his stripes we are healed
Genesis 1:1 - In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 18:32 - God is my strength and power
questions.explanation: Psalm 18:32 reflects the theme of divine strength provided to the upright, echoing Proverbs 10:29.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Proverbs 10:23 in the chapter?
options: Proverbs 10:22 - The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it
Proverbs 10:21 - The lips of the righteous feed many: but fools die for want of wisdom
Proverbs 10:24 - The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him
Proverbs 10:20 - The tongue of the just is as choice silver
questions.correctAnswer: Proverbs 10:22 - The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:22 directly precedes 10:23, providing context about the blessing of the LORD making rich without sorrow.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'yārēʾ' (ירא) used in Proverbs 10:27?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'yārēʾ' means fear or reverence, consistent with 'the fear of the LORD' in Proverbs 10:27.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Proverbs 10:31-32 contrasting the mouth of the just and the mouth of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:31-32 uses parallelism to contrast the wise speech of the just with the froward speech of the wicked.

questions.question: Does Proverbs 10:30 teach that the righteous will be permanently established in contrast to the wicked's fate?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:30 states, 'The righteous shall never be removed: but the wicked shall not inhabit the earth,' confirming permanent establishment for the righteous.

questions.question: Is it true that Proverbs 10:26 says a sluggard is like honey to the teeth and as smoke to the eyes?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:26 actually compares a sluggard to vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, not honey.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 10:2 teach about righteousness and human sin?
options: Righteousness delivers from death, while wicked treasures profit nothing
Wickedness leads to prosperity, but righteousness results in suffering
Both righteousness and wickedness yield equal reward
Wicked treasures provide eternal life, but righteousness leads to judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness delivers from death, while wicked treasures profit nothing
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:2 states that 'Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death,' teaching that righteousness secures true life, contrasting with the futility of wicked gain.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine provision and human diligence is taught in Proverbs 10:3?
options: The LORD sustains the righteous but removes the wealth of the wicked
God ignores the righteous and blesses the wicked with riches
Human effort alone secures provision without divine involvement
Both righteous and wicked receive equal provision from God
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD sustains the righteous but removes the wealth of the wicked
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:3 affirms that 'The LORD will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked,' showing God's providential care for the righteous and judgment on the wicked.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification and instruction is taught in Proverbs 10:17?
options: Keeping instruction leads to life, but refusing reproof leads to error
Instruction is irrelevant to life and sanctification
Refusing reproof is a sign of spiritual maturity
Life is independent of moral instruction and correction
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping instruction leads to life, but refusing reproof leads to error
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:17 teaches that 'He is in the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth,' emphasizing the role of correction in the process of sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 10:27 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:27 states, 'The fear of the LORD prolongeth days: but the years of the wicked shall be shortened,' demonstrating God's attribute of justice in rewarding the righteous and punishing the wicked.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Proverbs 10:22 regarding the blessing of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:22 says, 'The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it,' illustrating God's benevolent nature in giving blessings without adding trouble.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 10:6 connect to broader biblical themes of blessing and judgment?
options: It contrasts blessings on the just with the silencing of the wicked by violence, prefiguring God's final judgment
It teaches that all receive blessings regardless of moral standing
It denies any connection between righteousness and blessing
It asserts that violence is a blessing for the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts blessings on the just with the silencing of the wicked by violence, prefiguring God's final judgment
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:6 states 'Blessings are upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked,' connecting to biblical themes of divine blessing for the righteous and judgment upon the wicked.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 10:25 relate to the theme of divine justice and the eternal security of the righteous in Scripture?
options: The wicked will be swept away like a whirlwind, but the righteous stand as an everlasting foundation
Both the wicked and righteous have equal permanence on earth
The righteous are transient while the wicked remain eternally
Divine justice is indifferent to human conduct
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked will be swept away like a whirlwind, but the righteous stand as an everlasting foundation
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:25 teaches that 'As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is an everlasting foundation,' reflecting the biblical theme of the enduring security of the righteous versus the temporal fate of the wicked.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 10:1 and Proverbs 10:5 teach about wisdom and diligence in sanctification?
options: A wise and diligent son brings joy and shame is caused by laziness and folly
Folly and laziness are equally honored by God
Diligence is unnecessary for spiritual growth
Wisdom is inherited solely through family lineage
questions.correctAnswer: A wise and diligent son brings joy and shame is caused by laziness and folly
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:1 says 'A wise son maketh a glad father,' and 10:5 contrasts gathering in summer (wisdom) with sleeping in harvest (shame), showing the importance of wisdom and diligence in sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about speech and wisdom is taught in Proverbs 10:8 and Proverbs 10:31?
options: Wise hearts receive commandments and the mouth of the just produces wisdom
Fools are wiser than those who receive commandments
The mouth of the just leads to destruction
questions.correctAnswer: Wise hearts receive commandments and the mouth of the just produces wisdom
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:8 states 'The wise in heart will receive commandments,' and 10:31 says 'The mouth of the just bringeth forth wisdom,' teaching the connection between heart wisdom, obedience, and righteous speech.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about love and human sin is taught in Proverbs 10:12 and Proverbs 10:19?
options: Love covers all sins and restraint in speech is wisdom
Excessive speech is the mark of the righteous
Love provokes strife and should be avoided
questions.correctAnswer: Love covers all sins and restraint in speech is wisdom
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:12 teaches that 'Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins,' while 10:19 notes that 'In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise,' combining love and speech restraint as antidotes to sin.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Proverbs 10:24-25 teaches that the righteous will always avoid suffering, while the wicked will never prosper. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The fear of the wicked comes upon them, and they will be no more; the righteous are an everlasting foundation
The wicked prosper indefinitely, and the righteous suffer without relief
All people receive equal outcomes regardless of righteousness
God is indifferent to the fate of the wicked and righteous
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of the wicked comes upon them, and they will be no more; the righteous are an everlasting foundation
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:24-25 states, 'The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him: but the desire of the righteous shall be granted. As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is an everlasting foundation,' affirming divine justice rather than suggesting absolute temporal immunity from suffering.

questions.question: What doctrine about the relationship between wealth and security does Proverbs 10:15 teach?
options: The rich man's wealth is his strong city, while poverty leads to destruction for the poor
Poverty is a sign of divine favor
Both rich and poor have equal security regardless of their wealth
questions.correctAnswer: The rich man's wealth is his strong city, while poverty leads to destruction for the poor
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:15 states, 'The rich man's wealth is his strong city: the destruction of the poor is their poverty,' teaching a principle about the temporal security that wealth can provide, contrasting with the vulnerability of poverty.

questions.question: What divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Proverbs 10:29 about the LORD's way?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:29 states, 'The way of the LORD is strength to the upright,' highlighting God's attribute of strength as a support to those who walk righteously.

questions.question: How do Proverbs 10:7 and Proverbs 10:30 together contribute to the redemptive-historical theme of legacy and eternal dwelling?
options: The memory of the just is blessed and they shall never be removed, but the wicked’s name shall rot and they shall not inhabit the earth
Both the just and wicked have equally lasting legacies
The wicked inherit eternal dwelling, while the just are forgotten
Legacy is irrelevant to biblical theology
questions.correctAnswer: The memory of the just is blessed and they shall never be removed, but the wicked’s name shall rot and they shall not inhabit the earth
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:7 says, 'The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot,' and 10:30 affirms, 'The righteous shall never be removed: but the wicked shall not inhabit the earth,' together emphasizing the eternal security and remembrance of the righteous versus the ultimate removal of the wicked.

questions.question: What doctrine about human speech and divine wisdom is taught in Proverbs 10:13 and Proverbs 10:32?
options: Understanding brings wisdom to speech, but the mouth of the wicked speaks perversity
Fools speak wisely and the wicked teach righteousness
Speech has no connection to wisdom or wickedness
All speech is equally acceptable before God
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding brings wisdom to speech, but the mouth of the wicked speaks perversity
questions.explanation: Proverbs 10:13 states, 'In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found,' and 10:32 says, 'The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable: but the mouth of the wicked speaketh frowardness,' teaching the link between understanding, righteous speech, and wicked perversion.
